```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This vignette takes one pedigree from its records to a drawing. It reads the
example pedigree that comes with the package, checks it, numbers its
generations and family trees, computes kinship, trims it to one animal's
ancestors and draws them. Then it shrinks the pedigree and finds a set of
unrelated animals in it. The last section converts a kinship2 pedigree.

## A pedigree is a data frame

A pedigree has one row per animal: its `id`, `sire` and `dam` (`NA` for an
unknown parent; an animal may have one known parent), and optionally its `sex`
(`"M"`, `"F"`, `"H"` for a hermaphrodite or `"U"` for unknown), a `status`
(`"DECEASED"` marks an animal that has died) and condition columns, whose names
start with `affected`. Other columns are kept. Twins are listed in a table of
their own, one pair per row: `id1`, `id2` and `code` (`"MZ twin"`, `"DZ twin"`
or `"UZ twin"`, for identical, fraternal and unknown).

pedkindraw comes with a pedigree of 375 rhesus macaques and the table of its
three twin pairs. Both are files copied unchanged from the examples of the
package nprcgenekeepr, which disguised (obfuscated) the records for use in
examples.

```{r read}
library(pedkindraw)

pedFile <- system.file("extdata", "obfuscated_rhesus_mhc_ped.csv",
                       package = "pedkindraw")
twinFile <- system.file("extdata", "obfuscated_rhesus_mhc_twin_relations.csv",
                        package = "pedkindraw")
ped <- read.csv(pedFile, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
twins <- read.csv(twinFile, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
nrow(ped)
head(ped)
twins
```

Besides `id`, `sire`, `dam` and `sex`, the file gives each animal's
generation (`gen`), birth date, exit date and age. It has no `status` or
condition column, so the drawing below marks neither.

## Checking the records

`checkPedigree()` lists each problem it finds, one row per problem, and
changes nothing. It finds none in the example. `checkTwinRelations()` stops if
a twin pair is not possible, for instance MZ or DZ twins that do not share a
sire and a dam, and otherwise returns the table.

```{r check}
checkPedigree(ped)
twins <- checkTwinRelations(ped, twins)
```

Records with problems look like this. Here `s2` is the sire of `o2` but has
no row of its own, and `d1`, the dam of `o1` and `o2`, is recorded as male.

```{r problems}
records <- data.frame(
  id   = c("s1", "d1", "o1", "o2"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, "s1", "s2"),
  dam  = c(NA, NA, "d1", "d1"),
  sex  = c("M", "M", "F", "M")
)
checkPedigree(records)
```

`addParents()` adds a row for each sire or dam that has none, and marks the
rows in a `recordStatus` column. `correctParentSex()` sets the sex of each
sire recorded as female and each dam recorded as male. After both, the check
finds nothing.

```{r repair}
records <- addParents(records)
records$sex <- correctParentSex(records$id, records$sire, records$dam,
                                records$sex, records$recordStatus)
records
checkPedigree(records)
```

## Generations and family trees

`findGeneration()` numbers each animal's generation: 0 for a founder, an
animal with no known sire or dam, and one more than its later parent's for
every other. The layout and `kinship()` need these numbers. The example spans
nine generations, 0 to 8, and the numbers are the same as the file's own
`gen` column, which this line replaces.

```{r generations}
ped$gen <- findGeneration(ped$id, ped$sire, ped$dam)
table(ped$gen)
```

`findPedigreeNumber()` numbers the family trees: animals joined through their
sires and dams share a number. The example has five trees, one of 343 animals
and four of 3 to 13.

```{r families}
ped$family <- findPedigreeNumber(ped$id, ped$sire, ped$dam)
table(ped$family)
```

## Kinship

`kinship()` computes the kinship coefficient of every pair of animals: the
chance that an allele taken at random from one animal and an allele taken at
random from the other are identical by descent. An animal's coefficient with
itself is 0.5, or more when it is inbred. With `sparse = TRUE` it returns a
sparse matrix, which saves memory in a large pedigree.

```{r kinship}
k <- kinship(ped$id, ped$sire, ped$dam, ped$gen, twinRelations = twins)
dim(k)
k[c("E06FRB", "HV7LZ3", "8GSXTQ", "P844CW"),
  c("E06FRB", "HV7LZ3", "8GSXTQ", "P844CW")]
```

E06FRB and HV7LZ3 are identical (MZ) twins. The twins table gives them a
coefficient of 0.5, the same as each has with itself; without it they would
have 0.25, that of full siblings. 8GSXTQ and P844CW are fraternal (DZ) twins,
full siblings, at 0.25.

An animal whose sire and dam are related is inbred. The example has 29 such
animals.

```{r inbred}
sum(diag(k) > 0.5)
k[c("81MJXH", "H16XSK", "ED5PDV"), c("81MJXH", "H16XSK", "ED5PDV")]
```

One of them is ED5PDV. Its sire 81MJXH and its dam H16XSK are half siblings,
both offspring of YPHFHF, and their kinship coefficient is 0.125. So ED5PDV's
coefficient with itself is (1 + 0.125) / 2 = 0.5625.

## Trimming a pedigree to the animals of interest

`getProbandPedigree()` keeps the animals of interest, the probands, and all
of their ancestors. ED5PDV and its ancestors are 16 animals in five
generations, 8 of them founders.

```{r trim}
small <- getProbandPedigree(ped, "ED5PDV")
nrow(small)
```

`trimPedigree()` does the same, and with `removeUninformative = TRUE` it also
removes each founder that has only one offspring, again and again until none
is left. Such a founder changes no kinship coefficient among the animals
left. Here that leaves the four animals that make ED5PDV inbred: YPHFHF, its
offspring 81MJXH and H16XSK, and ED5PDV.

```{r core}
core <- trimPedigree(ped, "ED5PDV", removeUninformative = TRUE)
core[, c("id", "sire", "dam", "sex")]
```

## Drawing a pedigree

`makePedigreeMatingLayout()` places each animal and each mating of a
pedigree, and `drawPedigreeDiagram()` draws the layout as an interactive
graph. The layout can also take a twins table, a kinship matrix and layout
hints, which its help page describes.

```{r drawing, out.width = "100%"}
layout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(small)
drawPedigreeDiagram(layout)
```

Squares are males and circles females. The small dot between two animals is
their mating, and a line goes down from it to each of their offspring. The
mating of the half siblings 81MJXH and H16XSK is drawn in orange, because
their kinship coefficient is above 0. Three animals are drawn twice, and a
dashed line joins the two places of each: YPHFHF beside each of its two
mates, and 5LDNWE and H16XSK under their sire and dam and again beside their
mate. In the drawing you can zoom, hover over an animal to highlight the
animals joined to it, pick an animal in the "Select by id" box, and save the
picture with the "Export Diagram (PNG)" button. From a script,
`savePedigreeDiagram()` saves the drawing as an SVG, a PDF or a PNG file;
`vignette("drawing")` shows how.

## Shrinking a pedigree

`shrinkPedigree()` trims a pedigree to the animals needed to keep it
informative within a budget on its bit size, given which animals are
genotyped and, optionally, which are affected. It follows kinship2's
`pedigree.shrink()`. The bit size, which `bitSize()` gives, is twice the
number of animals with a known parent less the number of founders. The
example has no genotypes, so 30 percent of the animals are picked at random
to stand for the genotyped ones: 109 of the 375.

```{r genotyped}
set.seed(42)
genotyped <- runif(nrow(ped)) < 0.3
sum(genotyped)
bitSize(ped)
```

The whole pedigree's bit size is 2 * 251 - 124 = 378.

```{r shrink}
shrunk <- shrinkPedigree(ped, genotyped, maxBits = 16L)
lengths(shrunk$idList)
c(shrunk$pedSizeOriginal, shrunk$pedSizeIntermed, shrunk$pedSizeFinal)
shrunk$bitSize[c(1L, 2L, length(shrunk$bitSize))]
```

It works in steps. It first removes 104 unavailable animals: those not
genotyped that are left with no offspring, and founders that add nothing.
Then it removes 4 genotyped animals with no offspring left whose sire and dam
are both genotyped. That takes the pedigree from 375 animals to 267, and its
bit size from 378 to 237. Last, it removes one genotyped animal with no
offspring left at a time, each time the one whose removal leaves the smallest
bit size, with the animals that removal leaves unavailable, until the bit size
is at most 16. That takes 214 more animals and leaves 53, at a bit size of 16.
Its help page gives each rule.

## Finding unrelated animals

`findUnrelated()` chooses genotyped animals of which no two are related, as
many as it can: 44 of the 109 genotyped animals here. Their kinship
coefficients with each other are all 0.

```{r unrelated}
unrelated <- findUnrelated(ped, genotyped)
length(unrelated)
kU <- k[unrelated, unrelated]
all(kU[upper.tri(kU)] == 0)
```

```{r claims, include = FALSE}
## Each value the text above states, held here: the vignette stops
## building if one no longer holds.
stopifnot(
  nrow(ped) == 375L, nrow(twins) == 3L,
  !any(c("status", "affected") %in% names(ped)),
  nrow(checkPedigree(ped)) == 0L,
  identical(checkTwinRelations(ped, twins), twins)
)
problems <- checkPedigree(data.frame(
  id   = c("s1", "d1", "o1", "o2"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, "s1", "s2"),
  dam  = c(NA, NA, "d1", "d1"),
  sex  = c("M", "M", "F", "M")
))
stopifnot(
  identical(problems$check, c("rowlessParents", "maleDams")),
  identical(problems$id, c("s2", "d1")),
  identical(records$id, c("s1", "d1", "o1", "o2", "s2")),
  identical(records$sex, c("M", "F", "F", "M", "M")),
  identical(records$recordStatus, c(rep("original", 4L), "added")),
  nrow(checkPedigree(records)) == 0L
)
fileGen <- read.csv(pedFile, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)$gen
founder <- is.na(ped$sire) & is.na(ped$dam)
names(fileGen) <- ped$id
laterParent <- pmax(fileGen[ped$sire], fileGen[ped$dam], na.rm = TRUE)
stopifnot(
  all(ped$gen == fileGen),
  identical(sort(unique(ped$gen)), 0:8),
  all(ped$gen[founder] == 0L),
  all(ped$gen[!founder] == laterParent[!founder] + 1L),
  identical(as.vector(sort(table(ped$family), decreasing = TRUE)),
            c(343L, 13L, 11L, 5L, 3L))
)
kNoTwins <- kinship(ped$id, ped$sire, ped$dam, ped$gen)
stopifnot(
  identical(dim(k), c(375L, 375L)),
  all(diag(k) >= 0.5),
  methods::is(kinship(ped$id, ped$sire, ped$dam, ped$gen, sparse = TRUE),
              "sparseMatrix"),
  k["E06FRB", "HV7LZ3"] == 0.5, k["E06FRB", "E06FRB"] == 0.5,
  k["HV7LZ3", "HV7LZ3"] == 0.5, kNoTwins["E06FRB", "HV7LZ3"] == 0.25,
  identical(twins$code[twins$id1 == "E06FRB" & twins$id2 == "HV7LZ3"],
            "MZ twin"),
  identical(twins$code[twins$id1 == "8GSXTQ" & twins$id2 == "P844CW"],
            "DZ twin"),
  k["8GSXTQ", "P844CW"] == 0.25,
  ped$sire[ped$id == "8GSXTQ"] == ped$sire[ped$id == "P844CW"],
  ped$dam[ped$id == "8GSXTQ"] == ped$dam[ped$id == "P844CW"],
  sum(diag(k) > 0.5) == 29L,
  identical(ped$sire[ped$id == "ED5PDV"], "81MJXH"),
  identical(ped$dam[ped$id == "ED5PDV"], "H16XSK"),
  identical(ped$sire[ped$id %in% c("81MJXH", "H16XSK")],
            c("YPHFHF", "YPHFHF")),
  ped$dam[ped$id == "81MJXH"] != ped$dam[ped$id == "H16XSK"],
  k["81MJXH", "H16XSK"] == 0.125, k["ED5PDV", "ED5PDV"] == 0.5625
)
core$gen <- findGeneration(core$id, core$sire, core$dam)
kCore <- kinship(core$id, core$sire, core$dam, core$gen)
stopifnot(
  nrow(small) == 16L, "ED5PDV" %in% small$id,
  sum(is.na(small$sire) & is.na(small$dam)) == 8L,
  length(unique(small$gen)) == 5L,
  identical(trimPedigree(ped, "ED5PDV"), small),
  setequal(core$id, c("YPHFHF", "81MJXH", "H16XSK", "ED5PDV")),
  isTRUE(all.equal(kCore, k[core$id, core$id]))
)
## The drawing: no warning from the layout, the orange mating, the animals
## drawn twice, and one mating dot per sire and dam pair.
withCallingHandlers(
  makePedigreeMatingLayout(small),
  warning = function(w) stop("the layout warned: ", conditionMessage(w))
)
realId <- function(nodeId) {
  ifelse(nodeId %in% names(layout$duplicateToReal),
         unname(layout$duplicateToReal[nodeId]), nodeId)
}
rowOf <- function(nodeId) layout$nodes$y[match(nodeId, layout$nodes$id)]
dupOf <- function(id) names(layout$duplicateToReal)[layout$duplicateToReal == id]
orange <- layout$edges$color %in% "#D55E00"
matings <- unique(small[!is.na(small$sire), c("sire", "dam")])
animals <- layout$nodes[realId(layout$nodes$id) %in% small$id, ]
animalSex <- small$sex[match(realId(animals$id), small$id)]
stopifnot(
  setequal(realId(layout$edges$from[orange]), c("81MJXH", "H16XSK")),
  length(unique(layout$edges$to[orange])) == 1L,
  identical(sort(unname(layout$duplicateToReal)),
            sort(c("YPHFHF", "5LDNWE", "H16XSK"))),
  all(animals$shape[animalSex == "M"] == "square"),
  all(animals$shape[animalSex == "F"] == "dot"),
  sum(startsWith(layout$nodes$id, "__union_")) == nrow(matings),
  identical(sort(unique(small$dam[small$sire %in% "YPHFHF"])),
            c("5LDNWE", "WFGRY3")),
  rowOf(dupOf("5LDNWE")) == rowOf("YPHFHF"),
  rowOf(dupOf("H16XSK")) == rowOf("81MJXH"),
  rowOf(dupOf("YPHFHF")) == rowOf("WFGRY3"),
  identical(small$sire[small$id == "5LDNWE"], "WDBGPF"),
  rowOf("5LDNWE") > rowOf("WDBGPF"), rowOf("H16XSK") > rowOf("YPHFHF")
)
stopifnot(
  sum(genotyped) == 109L,
  identical(bitSize(ped), list(bitSize = 378L, nFounder = 124L,
                               nNonFounder = 251L)),
  identical(lengths(shrunk$idList),
            c(unavail = 104L, noninform = 4L, affected = 214L)),
  shrunk$pedSizeOriginal == 375L, shrunk$pedSizeIntermed == 267L,
  shrunk$pedSizeFinal == 53L, nrow(shrunk$ped) == 53L,
  shrunk$bitSize[1L] == 378, shrunk$bitSize[2L] == 237,
  shrunk$bitSize[length(shrunk$bitSize)] == 16,
  bitSize(shrunk$ped)$bitSize == 16L,
  all(genotyped[match(shrunk$idList$noninform, ped$id)]),
  all(genotyped[match(ped$sire[match(shrunk$idList$noninform, ped$id)],
                      ped$id)]),
  all(genotyped[match(ped$dam[match(shrunk$idList$noninform, ped$id)],
                      ped$id)]),
  length(unrelated) == 44L, all(unrelated %in% ped$id[genotyped]),
  all(kU[upper.tri(kU)] == 0)
)
```

## For kinship2 users

`asPedFrame()` converts a kinship2 `pedigree` or `pedigreeList`, or a
Pedixplorer `Pedigree`, to a list: the pedigree as a data frame (`ped`), its
twins table (`twinRelations`), its layout hints (`hints`) and its declared
matings (`matings`, from kinship2's relation code 4), each `NULL` when the
object has none. The chunks below run only when kinship2 is installed.
They convert family 2 of kinship2's `sample.ped`, 14 animals. kinship2 codes
sex as 1 and 2 and an unknown parent as 0; the data frame has `"M"`, `"F"` and
`NA`.

```{r kinship2, eval = requireNamespace("kinship2", quietly = TRUE)}
data("sample.ped", package = "kinship2")
fam2 <- sample.ped[sample.ped$ped == 2, ]
p <- kinship2::pedigree(id = fam2$id, dadid = fam2$father,
                        momid = fam2$mother, sex = fam2$sex,
                        affected = fam2$affected)
x <- asPedFrame(p)
head(x$ped)
```

The data frame then goes to the functions above, and `kinship()` gives the
same coefficients as kinship2's own `kinship()`.

```{r kinship2Kinship, eval = requireNamespace("kinship2", quietly = TRUE)}
x$ped$gen <- findGeneration(x$ped$id, x$ped$sire, x$ped$dam)
k2 <- kinship(x$ped$id, x$ped$sire, x$ped$dam, x$ped$gen)
all.equal(k2, kinship2::kinship(p)[x$ped$id, x$ped$id])
```

```{r kinship2Claims, include = FALSE, eval = requireNamespace("kinship2", quietly = TRUE)}
stopifnot(
  nrow(x$ped) == 14L, is.null(x$twinRelations), is.null(x$hints),
  identical(sort(unique(x$ped$sex)), c("F", "M")),
  all(fam2$sex %in% 1:2), any(fam2$father == 0),
  identical(is.na(x$ped$sire), fam2$father == 0),
  nrow(checkPedigree(x$ped)) == 0L,
  isTRUE(all.equal(k2, kinship2::kinship(p)[x$ped$id, x$ped$id]))
)
```

## Where next

`?pedkindraw` lists every function by what it does.
`vignette("drawing", package = "pedkindraw")` shows what a drawing shows and
how to change it, one feature at a time: the symbols and the legend,
conditions, twins, animals drawn twice, the two edge styles and layout
hints, among others. The help pages of `makePedigreeMatingLayout()` and
`drawPedigreeDiagram()` describe the twins table, the kinship matrix and the
layout hints the drawing takes.
